en: Which is the most formal way to ask for help?
“Could you please assist me?” is polite and uses formal words, with no slang.
Which is the most formal greeting for a letter to a head teacher?
Formal letters begin with “Dear” followed by the person’s title and surname.
A letter starts “Dear Sir or Madam”. Which ending is correct and formal?
When you do not know the person’s name, a formal letter ends with “Yours faithfully”.
Which is the most formal way to say “kids”?
“Children” is the standard, formal word. The others are slang.
Which is the most formal way to say “loads of”?
“A great deal of” suits formal writing. “Tons of” and “heaps of” are chatty.
Which is the most formal way to say “find out”?
“Discover” is formal. “Suss out” and “twig” are informal slang.
Which is the most formal way to finish “Where can I ___ a form?”
“Obtain” is a formal word for get. “Grab” and “nab” are casual.
Which is the most formal apology?
“We apologise for the delay” uses full words and no slang, so it is formal.
Which sentence is written in formal English?
I am writing to complain about the noise.
I’m dead annoyed about the noise.
The noise is doing my head in.
Formal English avoids slang like “dead annoyed” and “doing my head in”.
“Awesome” is a chatty word, so this sentence is informal.
Which is the most formal way to say “buy”?
“Purchase” is the formal word for buy.
Which is the most formal way to say “start”?
“Commence” is formal. “Kick off” and “get going” are everyday phrases.
Which is the most formal way to say “need”?
“Require” is the formal word for need.
Which is the most formal way to say “let us know”?
“Inform us” is formal. The other two are friendly, casual phrases.
Which sentence is the most formal?
We’ve ditched the meeting till later.
“Postponed” is a formal word and the sentence has no slang or shortened words.
Which is the most formal way to say “Thanks a lot!”?
“Thank you very much” is the formal way to thank someone.
Which is the best way to begin a formal speech?
“Good afternoon, everyone” is a polite, formal greeting.
Which is the most formal way to finish “The test was ___ difficult”?
“Somewhat” is formal. “Kinda” and “sorta” are slang spellings.
Which word would not suit a formal report?
“Gonna” is slang for “going to”, so it does not belong in formal writing.
Which word would not suit formal writing?
“Stuff” is a casual word. “Items” or “equipment” would be used instead.
Which is the most formal way to finish “Prices have ___”?
“Increased” is formal. The other two are lively, informal phrases.
Which is the most formal way to say “check out”?
“Examine” is the formal word. The others are slang.
Which ending suits an email to a business you do not know?
“Kind regards” is a polite, formal way to end an email.
Which notice is the most formal?
It uses the full form “cannot” and no slang, so it is the most formal.
Which is the most formal way to say “sort out”?
“Repair” is the formal word for mending something.
Which sentence suits a science report?
We got the water nice and hot.
A science report uses formal, exact language, such as a measured temperature.
Which greeting is the most informal?
“Hey!” is a casual greeting used with friends.
Which is the most formal way to finish “The bus will ___ at noon”?
“Depart” is the formal word for leave.
Which is the most formal way to finish “Please ___ the meeting”?
“Attend” is formal. “Show up” and “turn up” are everyday phrases.
Which word would not suit a formal letter?
“Awesome” is informal. “Grateful” and “sincerely” are often used in formal letters.

example.q_en: Which is the most formal way to ask for help?
example.why_en: “Could you please assist me?” is polite and uses formal words, with no slang.

en.title: Formal and informal
en.teach: Formal English is used in letters, reports and speeches: full words, no slang (I am writing to ask…). Informal English is for friends (Hiya, guess what!).
